page: UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-12xCPU-24GB is a Cloud Native server family instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It features an x86_64 architecture powered by an AMD EPYC 7542 processor with 12 vCPUs and 12 physical cores. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 2.0 GHz with a shared allocation model. It is equipped with 24.0 GB of system memory, yielding a resource density of 2.0 GB of RAM per core. No local storage or GPU hardware is bundled with this instance, and it includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Performance benchmarks indicate a clear trade-off between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The single-core CPU performance under stress-ng is positioned in the bottom 10% at 784.69, and Geekbench single-core scores are average at 1237.0. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 8209.0 and a PassMark CPU score of 22472.2. Memory bandwidth is stable, registering 60.68 GB/sec for large-block read operations and 40.05 GB/sec for large-block write operations.

Given the shared CPU allocation and the 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio, this server offers a cost-effective profile for multi-threaded, non-latency-critical workloads. It is well-suited for tasks such as static web serving, where it achieves a throughput of 9.63 GB/sec, and database operations, scoring 7680.56 on PassMark. It is also capable of handling basic text processing, software compilation, and lightweight multi-threaded decompression, though it is not recommended for single-threaded tasks or intensive LLM text generation.
description: The UpCloud CLOUDNATIVE-12xCPU-24GB is a KVM-based virtual server from the Cloud Native family, featuring 12 shared vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 7542 processor and 24.0 GB of RAM. Operating at 2.0 GHz, this x86_64 instance lacks local storage and GPU accelerators but includes one public IPv4 address. Benchmark data reveals a distinct trade-off: single-core performance is limited, placing in the bottom 10% for stress-ng, while multi-core metrics reach average tiers, highlighted by a PassMark CPU score of 22472.2 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 8209.0. Memory write bandwidth reaches 40.05 GB/sec. This resource configuration is highly cost-efficient for multi-threaded workloads that do not require dedicated CPU cores. It is best suited for static web serving, multi-threaded software compilation, database operations, and general-purpose background processing.
